extracted.intended_audience: organizations (boards, management, CFOs), preparers of financial filings, investors, lenders, and insurance underwriters
extracted.subtask_description: A principle-based framework and recommended disclosures for organizations to report climate-related governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics/targets in mainstream financial filings so investors, lenders, and insurers can assess and price climate-related risks and opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location of Disclosures (Mainstream financial filings)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Task Force recommends that preparers of climate-related financial disclosures provide such disclosures in their mainstream (i.e., public) annual financial filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose in accordance with national disclosure requirements; if elements are incompatible with national financial filing rules, disclose them in other official company reports issued at least annually, widely distributed and subject to internal governance processes similar to financial reporting. The Task Force expects governance processes to involve review by the chief financial officer and audit committee, as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance
rubrics_metrics.description: The organization’s governance around climate-related risks and opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe board oversight of climate-related issues, the role of management in assessing and managing these issues, and the processes used by the board and management to monitor and oversee climate-related risks and opportunities. Expect review and control processes similar to those used for public financial disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: The actual and potential impacts of climate-related risks and opportunities on the organization’s businesses, strategy, and financial planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose how climate-related issues affect business model, strategic objectives, and financial planning across different time horizons (short-, medium-, long-term). Include discussion of how strategies might change under different climate outcomes and the resilience of strategies to those outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk Management
rubrics_metrics.description: The processes used by the organization to identify, assess, and manage climate-related risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how climate-related risks are integrated into the organization’s overall risk management processes, how risks are prioritized, and which controls/mitigations are used. Provide information on identification, assessment, and monitoring approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metrics and Targets
rubrics_metrics.description: The metrics and targets used to assess and manage relevant climate-related risks and opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include quantitative metrics (e.g., GHG emissions - Scope 1, 2, and, where appropriate, Scope 3), targets, performance against targets, and other financial or non-financial metrics used to assess climate-related risk and opportunity (e.g., internal carbon price, investment needs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenario Analysis (Resilience of strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose the resilience of the organization’s strategy, taking into consideration different climate-related scenarios, including a 2° Celsius or lower scenario.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe scenarios used, assumptions, analytical approach, time horizons, and how scenario results inform strategy and financial planning. Acknowledge that practices will evolve and explain challenges and benefits of scenario analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorization of Climate-Related Risks (Transition and Physical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify and disclose climate-related risks as (1) risks related to the transition to a lower-carbon economy and (2) risks related to the physical impacts of climate change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For transition risks, discuss policy/legal, technology, market, and reputational risks; for physical risks, discuss acute (event-driven) and chronic (longer-term shifts) impacts and exposure across operations and supply chains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality Principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the principle of materiality when determining climate-related financial disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosures should focus on information material to investors, lenders and insurance underwriters. The Task Force encourages organizations where climate-related issues could be material in the future to begin disclosing outside financial filings to facilitate incorporation into filings once materiality is established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-usefulness (clarity, comparability, consistency, reliability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures should provide decision-useful, forward-looking information on financial impacts and be clear, comparable, consistent, and reliable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid boilerplate; provide context and explanation so users can assess financial implications. Align with existing standards where possible to improve comparability and consistency across organizations and jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and Alignment with Existing Frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: Draw on and align with existing climate-related disclosure frameworks and standards where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage frameworks such as CDSB, SASB, GRI, GHG Protocol, accounting standards, and other sector-specific guidance to avoid duplicative reporting and to facilitate comparability and usefulness to primary users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sector-Supplemental Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide supplemental, sector-specific guidance where necessary to highlight important sector considerations and potential financial impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial-sector organizations and certain non-financial sectors should use supplemental guidance to disclose fuller pictures of potential climate-related financial impacts relevant to their sector (e.g., asset owner/manager considerations).

rubrics_metrics.name: GHG Emissions Disclosure (Scope definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report greenhouse gas emissions using standard scope definitions: Scope 1 (direct), Scope 2 (indirect from purchased energy), and Scope 3 (other indirect value-chain emissions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where relevant and feasible, disclose Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions and explain methodologies, boundaries, calculation approaches, and limitations. Recognize challenges in data availability and quality for Scope 3 and investment-linked emissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal Carbon Price Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose whether an internal carbon price is used and how it is applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the internal carbon price’s role (planning tool, incentive for energy efficiency, guide for capital allocation), its level, assumptions, and how it affects investment and operational decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time Frames and Horizon Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose and use appropriate short, medium, and long-term time frames when assessing and reporting climate-related risks and opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify the time horizons used in strategy, scenario analysis, and financial planning; align them with business planning cycles and the nature of the risks/opportunities being assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Coverage and Organizational Boundaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly state the organizational ownership, scope of coverage, and boundaries used in disclosures (e.g., consolidation approach, subsidiaries, investments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about which entities, assets, and activities are included/excluded and rationale for the chosen consolidation approach to support comparability and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Availability, Quality, and Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose the availability and quality of underlying data used in climate-related financial disclosures and highlight limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document data sources, estimation methods, and any material data gaps; explain efforts to improve data quality and how limitations affect reported metrics and scenario analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remuneration and Incentive Alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider and disclose how remuneration and incentives are aligned with managing climate-related risks and opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report whether and how executive and other remuneration policies incorporate climate-related performance or risk management objectives, and any changes to incentives to support transition/resilience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider and disclose interactions between climate-related disclosures and applicable accounting standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address how climate-related issues may affect financial statements, provisioning, asset valuation, impairments, and other accounting treatments; coordinate disclosures with accounting statements where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of Costs and Benefits / Voluntariness
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop disclosures with an intent to balance the costs to preparers and the benefits to users; recommendations are voluntary and principle-based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design disclosure approaches that are practical for near-term adoption, scalable, and mindful of preparer burdens while providing decision-useful information to primary users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement and Ongoing Dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage ongoing stakeholder engagement and investor dialogue regarding climate-related financial disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicit and incorporate feedback from investors, lenders, insurers and other stakeholders during development and implementation of disclosures; expect disclosures to evolve based on feedback and practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about Methodologies and Assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Be transparent about methodologies, models, and key assumptions used to derive reported metrics and scenario outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient methodological detail so users can understand, replicate where possible, and evaluate the robustness of the conclusions and their sensitivity to assumptions.
